mission: Talon identifies Korda as old GAG security system in respectable clothing. Korda’s presence implies the Foundation is operationally compromised by old GAG-linked security and records access. Talon’s humor thins out — Korda makes Talon feel contaminated by his own past, not merely suspicious. Using Iressa’s tools, Talon submits a fake manifest correction / records query that makes it look as if a missing piece of the Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest has resurfaced. The signal is boring enough to look bureaucratic, but specific enough that anyone guarding the old shipment trail will notice. This is not just hacking. Talon uses the shape of his old compromised work as bait, putting an old version of himself back on the board.
why_now: Korda's presence at the Foundation confirmed the operational connection. To prove it is active rather than historical, Talon has to bait a response — submitting a fake manifest correction specific enough that anyone guarding the old shipment trail will notice, but boring enough to pass as routine records work. If Korda responds, the Foundation isn't just hiding history; it's guarding an active operation.
conflict: Talon uses the shape of his own old compromised work as bait — putting an old version of himself back on the board. Korda's presence makes Talon feel contaminated by his past, not merely suspicious. The bait-setting feels like re-entering the room that ruined his life because the only way to catch the people who put him there is to look like them again.
setting: Coruscant, Iressa's secondary cache (Talon submits the fake manifest correction here) and then the Foundation's external surface (where Korda responds, indirectly, through a courier dispatch). Mid-evening; the warehouse district is quiet; foot traffic is sparse.
emotional_trajectory: Korda should make Talon feel seen in the worst way. The bait-setting beat should feel like Talon willingly re-entering the room that ruined his life because the only way to catch the people who put him there is to look like them again. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: Plain-language consequence: if Korda responds, the Foundation is actively guarding the hidden shipment trail.

stakes.personal: Korda makes Talon feel seen in the worst possible way — seen and categorized and proven to be exactly what Tess always said he was. Talon's humor goes thin, not because he's afraid of Korda, but because Korda's presence means Talon's past is still running, still labeled, still readable by the right eyes.
stakes.interpersonal: Talon is doing this while Ben watches, which means Ben now sees Talon use the skills that got Talon convicted. Talon knows he's being watched. He does it anyway because the only way to catch the people who put him here is to look like them one more time.
stakes.external: If Korda responds to the fake manifest correction, the Foundation is actively guarding the hidden shipment trail — not preserving history, running an operation. Korda's indirect response confirms it. The Vigil is operational.

sensory_details: Iressa's secondary cache at mid-evening: the warehouse district has the quality of silence that comes from the absence of anything organic — no wind through gaps, just the low hum of climate infrastructure and foot traffic sparse enough to notice. Talon works at the terminal with the same body posture Ben has seen on his better moments — slightly forward, focused, the jokes turned off. The manifest correction he submits is forty-seven words of administrative language that reads like nothing. That's the point.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Korda responds indirectly — a courier dispatch, an unusual records query routed through Foundation channels, a specific pattern Talon reads as deliberate. The shape of the response identifies someone who knows exactly what bait looks like and is choosing to move anyway.
turning_point_detail.shift: The Foundation isn't preserving old GAG history. It's running an active operation. Korda's response is the confirmation that the Vigil is guarding the shipment trail in real time.
turning_point_detail.cost: Talon has just put an old version of himself back on the board — visible to anyone still watching his old authorization profile. He may have triggered something that moves faster than he intended.

emotional_arc.start: Talon is controlled and tightly focused — jokes turned off, working with the precision of someone who knows exactly how this records language is supposed to look.
emotional_arc.shift: Korda's presence earlier in the chapter makes the bait-setting feel less like a trap and more like Talon is the one being re-entered into a system he thought he'd escaped.
emotional_arc.end: Korda responds. Proof acquired. Talon is quieter than usual. He does not name what seeing Korda cost him, and Ben does not push.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon identifies Korda as old GAG security infrastructure in a clean professional suit; his humor thins visibly.
key_beats.state_change: Korda's presence shifts the Foundation from suspicious to operationally compromised — this is not preserved history, it is active infrastructure.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Talon's jokes turning off is its own kind of signal — Ben registering the thinning as more informative than the identification.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon constructs a fake manifest correction using Iressa's tools — forty-seven words of administrative language designed to look routine but flag specifically to anyone still watching the old shipment trail.
key_beats.state_change: The bait is set: an old version of Talon is back on the board, visible to the same system that categorized and ruined him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Talon working with his jokes fully off — the body posture forward, focused — and the quality of watching someone do something they swore they wouldn't do again.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben watches Talon work with the skills that got Talon convicted; neither of them names what that means.
key_beats.state_change: The collaboration now includes Ben witnessing Talon's compromised professional past being deployed deliberately.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Not looking away — the choice to witness it straight — and the discomfort of being the one being trusted to do that.

key_beats.beat_description: Korda responds indirectly — a courier dispatch, a routing pattern, a shape Talon reads as deliberate rather than coincidental.
key_beats.state_change: The Foundation is confirmed as actively guarding the shipment trail in real time — not preserving old records but running a live operation.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The confirmation arriving without announcement — Talon naming the response pattern in one sentence, then going quiet.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon reads the response pattern as Korda choosing to move despite recognizing what the bait looked like.
key_beats.state_change: The Vigil is operational — Korda's response confirms the active operation rather than the archival interest.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The specific flatness that follows proof — not relief, the thing on the other side of certainty.
